evidence: find-all-orders.service.ts: FindAllOrdersService.findAll() delegates to ordersRepository.findAllOrders() and returns Promise<Order[]>

update-order.service.ts: UpdateOrderService.updateOrder loads the order through ordersRepository.findOrderByIdWithDeliveryman, calls the domain methods order.changeStatus and order.addInfoToDescription, then saves through ordersRepository.save
All three files constructor-inject OrdersRepository and use the Order model from src/delivery/__models__/orders.model, so they share one set of abstractions
Note (outside this rule): update-order.service.ts writes `updateOrderDto.isActive !== undefined ?? order.changeStatus(...)`, and the right side of `??` never runs, so the update has no effect
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module has three small application services, and all of them handle Order reads and updates. They share the same abstractions: each injects OrdersRepository through the constructor and returns the Order model. FindOneOrderService and UpdateOrderService both load an order by calling ordersRepository.findOrderByIdWithDeliveryman. That is shared use of one repository method, not a copied business rule. UpdateOrderService leaves state changes to the domain methods order.changeStatus and order.addInfoToDescription rather than changing fields directly, so it does not bypass the module's abstractions. None of the files split into an unrelated concern, duplicate an invariant or bypass the repository.

Outside this rule, update-order.service.ts has a correctness bug. It uses `updateOrderDto.isActive !== undefined ?? order.changeStatus(...)`. The left side of `??` is always a boolean, never null or undefined, so the right side never runs. As a result the domain methods are never called and the update does nothing. The service also does not handle a null order. These are behavior defects, not cohesion problems, so they do not affect this verdict, but they should be fixed.
